<h2><span id="What_is_Perplexity_AI_and_how_does_it_work"><strong>What is Perplexity AI and how does it work?</strong></span></h2>
<p><b>Perplexity is an AI-powered search engine. It acts as a bridge between you and the Internet, taking your question or query and generating a custom answer based on the information it finds on the web. </b></p>
<p><span style="font-weight: 400;">Perplexity AI is designed to completely streamline and personalise the experience of searching for information online. As described on the Perplexity website, it’s like having “a really smart friend who can quickly find and summarise information for you from all over the Internet.”</span></p>
<p><span style="font-weight: 400;">To use Perplexity AI, you type your question or search query into the text box, for example: “Best plant-based protein sources” (just as you would if you wanted to search Google or a similar search engine).</span></p>
<p><span style="font-weight: 400;">Perplexity then searches the Internet and generates an answer based on multiple sources across the web. It also shows you the top sources available on this topic, provides in-line citations so you can see where each fact or piece of information came from, and suggests a list of related questions or searches. Click on any of these related topics and Perplexity AI will generate another answer accordingly.</span></p>

<h3><span id="What_is_the_technology_behind_Perplexity_AI"><strong>What is the technology behind Perplexity AI?</strong></span></h3>
<p><span style="font-weight: 400;">Perplexity AI uses Natural Language Processing (NLP) to understand user queries and the context surrounding them. It also uses large language models (LLMs) like GPT-4, Claude, and its own proprietary models to generate human-like responses and summaries based on the information it finds online. </span></p>
<p><span style="font-weight: 400;">If you have a Perplexity Pro account, you can customise your account settings to choose which AI models are used for certain functions. For example, under the ‘AI model’ setting, you can choose from a range of options including Default, Experimental, GPT-4, Claude, and Gemini Pro.</span></p>
<h2><span id="What_can_Perplexity_AI_do_Key_features"><strong>What can Perplexity AI do? Key features</strong></span></h2>
<p><span style="font-weight: 400;">Perplexity AI is an all-powerful search assistant. It can answer questions, help you conduct research, generate new text content in different formats (e.g. code, emails, lists, and poems) and summarise articles and web pages. </span></p>
<p><span style="font-weight: 400;">We’ll explore some specific use cases a bit later on. First, let’s briefly introduce Perplexity AI’s key features. </span></p>
<p><span style="font-weight: 400;">The following features are available with the free version of Perplexity AI:</span><b></b></p>
<ul>
<li aria-level="1"><b>Search: </b><span style="font-weight: 400;">This is Perplexity AI’s core functionality. Enter your question, prompt, or query and the AI will generate a custom answer based on a variety of sources across the web.</span><span style="font-weight: 400;"><br>
</span></li>
</ul>
<ul>
<li aria-level="1"><b>Focus: </b><span style="font-weight: 400;">When entering a query, you can use the Focus feature to determine what kind of sources you want the AI to consult. For example, you can select ‘All’ to search the Internet in its entirety, or select ‘Academic’ to focus your search on published academic papers. If you just want the AI to generate a response without searching the web, set the Focus to ‘Writing’. </span></li>
</ul>

<p><b>Threads and Collections: </b><span style="font-weight: 400;">A Thread refers to a back-and-forth conversation you have with Perplexity. If you search for plant-based protein sources, then ask follow-up questions, that counts as one Thread. You can create Collections to store and organise related Threads, accessible via the ‘Library’ tab. </span></p>

<p><b>Discover:</b><span style="font-weight: 400;"> The Discover tab houses a built-in news feed, showcasing the latest news items and articles. Click on an article of interest and it’ll open up within the Perplexity AI interface. </span></p>
<p><img decoding="async" class="aligncenter wp-image-10503 size-full" src="data:image/svg+xml,%3Csvg%20xmlns='http://www.w3.org/2000/svg'%20viewBox='0%200%20938%20560'%3E%3C/svg%3E" alt="Perplexity AI showing the Discover feature" width="938" height="560" title="What is Perplexity AI and how can you use it in the design process? 6" data-lazy-src="https://www.uxdesigninstitute.com/blog/wp-content/uploads/2024/06/Screenshot-2024-06-14-at-11.46.07.png"><noscript><img loading="lazy" decoding="async" class="aligncenter wp-image-10503 size-full" src="https://www.uxdesigninstitute.com/blog/wp-content/uploads/2024/06/Screenshot-2024-06-14-at-11.46.07.png" alt="Perplexity AI showing the Discover feature" width="938" height="560" title="What is Perplexity AI and how can you use it in the design process? 6"></noscript></p>

<li aria-level="1"><b>Image generation: </b><span style="font-weight: 400;">With Perplexity Pro, you can enrich the AI’s response to your search queries with custom-generated images. </ul>
<h2><span id="Is_Perplexity_AI_better_than_ChatGPT"><strong>Is Perplexity AI better than ChatGPT?</strong></span></h2>
<p><span style="font-weight: 400;">Perplexity AI is better for conducting research. With access to the Internet, it can analyse a variety of sources to generate custom answers based on up-to-date information. It also includes in-line citations to show you where the information came from. </span></p>
<p><span style="font-weight: 400;">But, when it comes to conversational flow and generating unique content, ChatGPT still comes out on top. </span></p>
<p><span style="font-weight: 400;">Ultimately, whether you choose Perplexity AI or ChatGPT (or a combination of both) depends on your goals. If you want to streamline the process of conducting research and learning about different topics, or want a more personalised search experience, Perplexity AI would be your tool of choice. If you want help with ideation and content generation in a variety of formats, ChatGPT would likely still be your go-to. </span></p>
<p><span style="font-weight: 400;">Both tools offer free plans, so you don’t necessarily need to choose one or the other. It’s worth experimenting with both ChatGPT and Perplexity side-by-side to figure out which tool is best suited to various tasks. </span></p>
<p><span style="font-weight: 400;">With that, let’s consider how UX designers can use Perplexity AI. But first: a quick tutorial on how to get set up.</span></p>

<p><span style="font-weight: 400;">Want to supercharge your UX workflow? <h3><span id="1_Draft_interview_and_survey_questions_with_Perplexity_AI"><strong>1. Draft interview and survey questions with Perplexity AI</strong></span></h3>
<p><span style="font-weight: 400;">If you want to </span><a href="https://www.uxdesigninstitute.com/blog/user-interviews-for-ux-research/"><span style="font-weight: 400;">conduct effective user interviews</span></a><span style="font-weight: 400;"> as part of your UX research, or send out </span><a href="https://www.uxdesigninstitute.com/blog/user-surveys-for-ux-research/"><span style="font-weight: 400;">user surveys</span></a><span style="font-weight: 400;">, you’ll need a strong set of questions. With the Focus feature set to ‘Writing’, you can use Perplexity to generate a list of suitable questions to include in your research. Here’s how:</span></p>
<p><span style="font-weight: 400;">Step 1: Navigate to the Perplexity homepage and set the Focus to ‘Writing’. </span></p>
<p><img decoding="async" class="aligncenter wp-image-10508 size-full" src="data:image/svg+xml,%3Csvg%20xmlns='http://www.w3.org/2000/svg'%20viewBox='0%200%20912%20480'%3E%3C/svg%3E" alt="Perplexity AI showing how to choose the Writing feature" width="912" height="480" title="What is Perplexity AI and how can you use it in the design process? 9" data-lazy-src="https://www.uxdesigninstitute.com/blog/wp-content/uploads/2024/06/Screenshot-2024-06-14-at-12.08.06.png"><noscript><img loading="lazy" decoding="async" class="aligncenter wp-image-10508 size-full" src="https://www.uxdesigninstitute.com/blog/wp-content/uploads/2024/06/Screenshot-2024-06-14-at-12.08.06.png" alt="Perplexity AI showing how to choose the Writing feature" width="912" height="480" title="What is Perplexity AI and how can you use it in the design process? 9"></noscript><span style="font-weight: 400;">Step 2: Provide context for the research you’re conducting and prompt the AI to draft a set of questions. Remember to include any relevant guidance as to how the questions should be formulated—for example, specify whether the questions should be open-ended or closed, and prompt the AI to use clear, straightforward, and inclusive language. </span></p>
<p><img decoding="async" class="aligncenter wp-image-10509 size-full" src="data:image/svg+xml,%3Csvg%20xmlns='http://www.w3.org/2000/svg'%20viewBox='0%200%20912%20564'%3E%3C/svg%3E" alt="Perplexity AI showing how to generate relevant research questions" width="912" height="564" title="What is Perplexity AI and how can you use it in the design process? 10" data-lazy-src="https://www.uxdesigninstitute.com/blog/wp-content/uploads/2024/06/Screenshot-2024-06-14-at-12.10.11.png"><noscript><img loading="lazy" decoding="async" class="aligncenter wp-image-10509 size-full" src="https://www.uxdesigninstitute.com/blog/wp-content/uploads/2024/06/Screenshot-2024-06-14-at-12.10.11.png" alt="Perplexity AI showing how to generate relevant research questions" width="912" height="564" title="What is Perplexity AI and how can you use it in the design process? 10"></noscript></p>
<p><span style="font-weight: 400;">Step 3: Press the → button to run the query and generate a list of questions. The output will look something like this:</span></p>

<p><span style="font-weight: 400;">Step 4: Use the ‘Share’ button to share the questions with your team for review, or use the ‘Copy’ function to copy-paste them into a separate doc. If you’re not happy with the output, try a follow-up prompt. </span></p>
<h3><span id="2_Use_Perplexity_AI_to_conduct_competitor_research"><strong>2. Use Perplexity AI to conduct competitor research </strong></span></h3>
<p><span style="font-weight: 400;">Perhaps you want to kick-start your next design project with some competitor analysis. With its advanced research capabilities, Perplexity AI can be a great help here. </span></p>
<p><span style="font-weight: 400;">Consider using it to identify your main competitors and compare their main features. This is useful for highlighting gaps in the market and getting inspiration for your own product. </span></p>
<p><span style="font-weight: 400;">Let’s give it a go, continuing with our plant-based recipe app example. </span></p>
<p><span style="font-weight: 400;">Step 1: We’ll start by identifying the top 10 competitors. Type your request into the designated search box, providing relevant context. For example: </span><b><i>I’m designing a plant-based recipe app and would like to conduct some competitor research. Can you identify the top ten competitors in this space (the most popular plant-based recipe apps or websites on the market) along with their key features and value propositions? Please present the results in a table.</i></b><b><i><br>

<h3><span id="3_Analyse_your_competitors_reviews_and_online_mentions"><strong>3. Analyse your competitors’ reviews and online mentions</strong></span></h3>
<p><span style="font-weight: 400;">Here’s another Perplexity hack to level up your competitor research: use it to read and summarise user reviews online. </span></p>
<p><span style="font-weight: 400;">This is a quick way to gain insight into what users are saying about your competitors, helping you identify your target users’ pain-points and frustrations. Let’s give it a go. </span></p>
<p><span style="font-weight: 400;">Step 1: Start a new Thread and make sure the Focus is set to ‘All’. Choose the first competitor you want to focus on and prompt the AI to analyse online reviews. If you’re analysing an app, prompt the AI to look at app store reviews, like so: </span><b><i>Please can you analyse app store reviews for the Oh She Glows plant-based recipe app and summarise the main positives and negatives that users mention?</i></b></p>
<p><img decoding="async" class="aligncenter wp-image-10516 size-full" src="data:image/svg+xml,%3Csvg%20xmlns='http://www.w3.org/2000/svg'%20viewBox='0%200%20922%20368'%3E%3C/svg%3E" alt=" Perplexity AI showing how to analyse reviews for a product" width="922" height="368" title="What is Perplexity AI and how can you use it in the design process? 16" data-lazy-src="https://www.uxdesigninstitute.com/blog/wp-content/uploads/2024/06/Screenshot-2024-06-14-at-12.29.03.png"><noscript><img loading="lazy" decoding="async" class="aligncenter wp-image-10516 size-full" src="https://www.uxdesigninstitute.com/blog/wp-content/uploads/2024/06/Screenshot-2024-06-14-at-12.29.03.png" alt=" Perplexity AI showing how to analyse reviews for a product" width="922" height="368" title="What is Perplexity AI and how can you use it in the design process? 16"></noscript></p>
<p><span style="font-weight: 400;">This gives us the following output—a list of the positives and negatives, with in-line citations linking to the original source.</span></p>
<p><img decoding="async" class="aligncenter wp-image-10517 size-full" src="data:image/svg+xml,%3Csvg%20xmlns='http://www.w3.org/2000/svg'%20viewBox='0%200%20914%20734'%3E%3C/svg%3E" alt=" showing an analysis of user reviews for a product" width="914" height="734" title="What is Perplexity AI and how can you use it in the design process? 17" data-lazy-src="https://www.uxdesigninstitute.com/blog/wp-content/uploads/2024/06/Screenshot-2024-06-14-at-12.31.52.png"><noscript><img loading="lazy" decoding="async" class="aligncenter wp-image-10517 size-full" src="https://www.uxdesigninstitute.com/blog/wp-content/uploads/2024/06/Screenshot-2024-06-14-at-12.31.52.png" alt=" showing an analysis of user reviews for a product" width="914" height="734" title="What is Perplexity AI and how can you use it in the design process? 17"></noscript></p>
<p><span style="font-weight: 400;">Step 2: Next, we can use Perplexity AI to search Reddit for user mentions of specific apps and websites. Start a new Thread, set the Focus to ‘Reddit’, and enter your prompt. For example: </span><b><i>Can you search for any mentions of the following websites/apps and summarise them into positives and negatives? Rainbow Plant Life, It Doesn’t Taste Like Chicken, Cookie & Kate.</i></b></p>
<p><img decoding="async" class="aligncenter wp-image-10518 size-full" src="data:image/svg+xml,%3Csvg%20xmlns='http://www.w3.org/2000/svg'%20viewBox='0%200%20920%20358'%3E%3C/svg%3E" alt="showing how to gather and analyse user reviews from Reddit" width="920" height="358" title="What is Perplexity AI and how can you use it in the design process? 18" data-lazy-src="https://www.uxdesigninstitute.com/blog/wp-content/uploads/2024/06/Screenshot-2024-06-14-at-12.34.16.png"><noscript><img loading="lazy" decoding="async" class="aligncenter wp-image-10518 size-full" src="https://www.uxdesigninstitute.com/blog/wp-content/uploads/2024/06/Screenshot-2024-06-14-at-12.34.16.png" alt="showing how to gather and analyse user reviews from Reddit" width="920" height="358" title="What is Perplexity AI and how can you use it in the design process? 18"></noscript></p>
<p><span style="font-weight: 400;">Again, we get a summary of any positive and negative mentions of the websites we specified, together with links to online sources (in this case, relevant Reddit threads):</span></p>
<p><img decoding="async" class="aligncenter wp-image-10519 size-full" src="data:image/svg+xml,%3Csvg%20xmlns='http://www.w3.org/2000/svg'%20viewBox='0%200%20916%20886'%3E%3C/svg%3E" alt="Perplexity AI showing an analysis of user reviews sourced from Reddit" width="916" height="886" title="What is Perplexity AI and how can you use it in the design process? 19" data-lazy-src="https://www.uxdesigninstitute.com/blog/wp-content/uploads/2024/06/Screenshot-2024-06-14-at-12.35.54.png"><noscript><img loading="lazy" decoding="async" class="aligncenter wp-image-10519 size-full" src="https://www.uxdesigninstitute.com/blog/wp-content/uploads/2024/06/Screenshot-2024-06-14-at-12.35.54.png" alt="Perplexity AI showing an analysis of user reviews sourced from Reddit" width="916" height="886" title="What is Perplexity AI and how can you use it in the design process? 19"></noscript></p>
<p><span style="font-weight: 400;">The effectiveness of this technique ultimately depends on how well-known your competitors are, and whether there are enough reviews and mentions online to provide insight into user sentiment. But, as with any AI hack, it’s a good springboard from which to kickstart your competitor research—not an all-encompassing solution. </span></p>
<h3><span id="4_Research_design_patterns_guidelines_and_best_practices"><strong>4. Research design patterns, guidelines, and best practices</strong></span></h3>
<p><span style="font-weight: 400;">With Perplexity AI on hand, you can quickly research any topic, expand your knowledge, and access information and best practices to help you in your work. Let’s consider some different prompts you might use to make the most of Perplexity’s research and knowledge-summarising capabilities.</span></p>
<p><span style="font-weight: 400;">Step 1: Let’s say you’re designing a mobile app and want to learn about </span><a href="https://www.uxdesigninstitute.com/blog/card-design-for-ui/"><span style="font-weight: 400;">card design</span></a><span style="font-weight: 400;"> best practices. Open a new Thread, set the Focus to ‘All’ (so Perplexity searches all sources on the web), and type something like: </span><b><i>Can you tell me about card design for mobile apps, with best practices and examples?</i></b></p>
<p><img decoding="async" class="aligncenter wp-image-10521 size-full" src="data:image/svg+xml,%3Csvg%20xmlns='http://www.w3.org/2000/svg'%20viewBox='0%200%20924%20336'%3E%3C/svg%3E" alt="Perplexity AI showing how to research for card design" width="924" height="336" title="What is Perplexity AI and how can you use it in the design process? 20" data-lazy-src="https://www.uxdesigninstitute.com/blog/wp-content/uploads/2024/06/Screenshot-2024-06-14-at-12.38.37.png"><noscript><img loading="lazy" decoding="async" class="aligncenter wp-image-10521 size-full" src="https://www.uxdesigninstitute.com/blog/wp-content/uploads/2024/06/Screenshot-2024-06-14-at-12.38.37.png" alt="Perplexity AI showing how to research for card design" width="924" height="336" title="What is Perplexity AI and how can you use it in the design process? 20"></noscript></p>
<p><span style="font-weight: 400;">Perplexity gives you a concise bullet-point summary based on a variety of blog posts, together with familiar examples:</span></p>
<p><img decoding="async" class="aligncenter wp-image-10522 size-full" src="data:image/svg+xml,%3Csvg%20xmlns='http://www.w3.org/2000/svg'%20viewBox='0%200%20912%20504'%3E%3C/svg%3E" alt="Perplexity AI showing output for card design examples" width="912" height="504" title="What is Perplexity AI and how can you use it in the design process? 21" data-lazy-src="https://www.uxdesigninstitute.com/blog/wp-content/uploads/2024/06/Screenshot-2024-06-14-at-12.40.38.png"><noscript><img loading="lazy" decoding="async" class="aligncenter wp-image-10522 size-full" src="https://www.uxdesigninstitute.com/blog/wp-content/uploads/2024/06/Screenshot-2024-06-14-at-12.40.38.png" alt="Perplexity AI showing output for card design examples" width="912" height="504" title="What is Perplexity AI and how can you use it in the design process? 21"></noscript></p>
<p><span style="font-weight: 400;">Step 2: Based on the specifics of your project, you could then ask a follow-up question such as: </span><b><i>How could I use card design when creating the UI for a plant-based recipe app?</i></b></p>
<p><img decoding="async" class="aligncenter wp-image-10523 size-full" src="data:image/svg+xml,%3Csvg%20xmlns='http://www.w3.org/2000/svg'%20viewBox='0%200%20920%20520'%3E%3C/svg%3E" alt="Screenshot of Perplexity AI showing how to generate UI ideas" width="920" height="520" title="What is Perplexity AI and how can you use it in the design process? 22" data-lazy-src="https://www.uxdesigninstitute.com/blog/wp-content/uploads/2024/06/Screenshot-2024-06-14-at-12.44.52.png"><noscript><img loading="lazy" decoding="async" class="aligncenter wp-image-10523 size-full" src="https://www.uxdesigninstitute.com/blog/wp-content/uploads/2024/06/Screenshot-2024-06-14-at-12.44.52.png" alt="Screenshot of Perplexity AI showing how to generate UI ideas" width="920" height="520" title="What is Perplexity AI and how can you use it in the design process? 22"></noscript></p>
<p><span style="font-weight: 400;">Step 3: Let’s try another example. This time, you want to make sure that the product you’re designing is both accessible and inclusive. In a new Thread, try a prompt such as: </span><b><i>I’m designing a mobile app and I want to make sure it’s as accessible and inclusive as possible. Can you create a checklist I can run through when designing my app?</i></b><b><i><br>
</i></b><b><i><br>
</i></b><span style="font-weight: 400;">Within seconds, you’ve got an overview of various factors you should consider, together with links to external sources if you’d like to learn more.</span></p>
<p><img decoding="async" class="aligncenter wp-image-10524 size-full" src="data:image/svg+xml,%3Csvg%20xmlns='http://www.w3.org/2000/svg'%20viewBox='0%200%20916%20838'%3E%3C/svg%3E" alt="showing how to generate accessibility and inclusivity ideas checklist" width="916" height="838" title="What is Perplexity AI and how can you use it in the design process? 23" data-lazy-src="https://www.uxdesigninstitute.com/blog/wp-content/uploads/2024/06/Screenshot-2024-06-14-at-12.52.41.png"><noscript><img loading="lazy" decoding="async" class="aligncenter wp-image-10524 size-full" src="https://www.uxdesigninstitute.com/blog/wp-content/uploads/2024/06/Screenshot-2024-06-14-at-12.52.41.png" alt="showing how to generate accessibility and inclusivity ideas checklist" width="916" height="838" title="What is Perplexity AI and how can you use it in the design process? 23"></noscript></p>

<h3><span id="5_Use_Perplexity_AI_to_find_and_compare_tools"><span style="font-size: 18pt;"><strong>5. Use Perplexity AI to find and compare tools</strong></span></span></h3>
<p><span style="font-weight: 400;">Need to find the </span><a href="https://www.uxdesigninstitute.com/blog/ui-ux-design-tools/"><span style="font-weight: 400;">best UX design tools</span></a><span style="font-weight: 400;"> for a particular task, or the best software to help your team be more efficient? Use Perplexity AI to compare different options and find the most fitting tool for the job.</span></p>
<p>Step 1: <span style="font-weight: 400;">Open a new Thread, with the Focus set to ‘All’. Then enter your prompt depending on the tools you’re looking for. For example: </span><b><i>I’m looking for a new prototyping tool to help my UX design team work more collaboratively. We’re a distributed team who works remote. Can you help me compare the best prototyping tools around, comparing factors such as price, pros and cons, and key features?</i></b></p>
<p><img decoding="async" class="aligncenter wp-image-10525 size-full" src="data:image/svg+xml,%3Csvg%20xmlns='http://www.w3.org/2000/svg'%20viewBox='0%200%20932%20620'%3E%3C/svg%3E" alt="Perplexity AI showing how to find and compare tools" width="932" height="620" title="What is Perplexity AI and how can you use it in the design process? 24" data-lazy-src="https://www.uxdesigninstitute.com/blog/wp-content/uploads/2024/06/Screenshot-2024-06-14-at-13.02.23.png"><noscript><img loading="lazy" decoding="async" class="aligncenter wp-image-10525 size-full" src="https://www.uxdesigninstitute.com/blog/wp-content/uploads/2024/06/Screenshot-2024-06-14-at-13.02.23.png" alt="Perplexity AI showing how to find and compare tools" width="932" height="620" title="What is Perplexity AI and how can you use it in the design process? 24"></noscript></p>
<p> </p>
<p>Step 2: <span style="font-weight: 400;">Perplexity gives you a straightforward list of </span><a href="https://www.uxdesigninstitute.com/blog/best-prototyping-tools-for-ux-designers/"><span style="font-weight: 400;">recommended prototyping tools</span></a><span style="font-weight: 400;">, but you might find it easier to compare the results in a table. If so, follow up with this prompt: </span><b><i>Can you present the results in a table please for ease of comparison?</i></b></p>
<p><img decoding="async" class="aligncenter wp-image-10526 size-full" src="data:image/svg+xml,%3Csvg%20xmlns='http://www.w3.org/2000/svg'%20viewBox='0%200%20932%20930'%3E%3C/svg%3E" alt="Perplexity AI showing output for prototyping tools" width="932" height="930" title="What is Perplexity AI and how can you use it in the design process? 25" data-lazy-srcset="https://www.uxdesigninstitute.com/blog/wp-content/uploads/2024/06/Screenshot-2024-06-14-at-13.04.00.png 932w, https://www.uxdesigninstitute.com/blog/wp-content/uploads/2024/06/Screenshot-2024-06-14-at-13.04.00-150x150.png 150w" data-lazy-sizes="auto, (max-width: 932px) 100vw, 932px" data-lazy-src="https://www.uxdesigninstitute.com/blog/wp-content/uploads/2024/06/Screenshot-2024-06-14-at-13.04.00.png"><noscript><img loading="lazy" decoding="async" class="aligncenter wp-image-10526 size-full" src="https://www.uxdesigninstitute.com/blog/wp-content/uploads/2024/06/Screenshot-2024-06-14-at-13.04.00.png" alt="Perplexity AI showing output for prototyping tools" width="932" height="930" title="What is Perplexity AI and how can you use it in the design process? 25" srcset="https://www.uxdesigninstitute.com/blog/wp-content/uploads/2024/06/Screenshot-2024-06-14-at-13.04.00.png 932w, https://www.uxdesigninstitute.com/blog/wp-content/uploads/2024/06/Screenshot-2024-06-14-at-13.04.00-150x150.png 150w" sizes="auto, (max-width: 932px) 100vw, 932px"></noscript></p>
<p><span style="font-weight: 400;">Note that, in this example, Perplexity only compares three tools. In such cases, you’d want to click on one of the suggested sources to find a more comprehensive tool comparison. </span></p>
<p><span style="font-weight: 400;">This example also highlights an important point regarding accuracy and reliability. Perplexity suggests InVision as a prototyping tool worth considering—but, at the time of writing, InVision is in the process of shutting down (with all InVision services planned to be closed by the end of 2024). As such, this isn’t a great suggestion for someone looking for a new tool. <strong>A good reminder to verify, fact-check, and do your own research when using AI.</strong></span></p>
<h2><span id="The_takeaway"><strong>The takeaway </strong></span></h2>
<p><span style="font-weight: 400;">Perplexity AI is an incredibly powerful research tool. It can analyse online journals, web pages, and articles in seconds, summarise key information, and generate a custom response to any question or prompt. </span></p>
<p><span style="font-weight: 400;">This can help to streamline many different aspects of the UX design process—from identifying and analysing competitor products, drafting user interview and survey questions, quickly getting to grips with specific </span><a href="https://www.uxdesigninstitute.com/blog/ux-design-principles/"><span style="font-weight: 400;">UX design principles</span></a><span style="font-weight: 400;">, finding and comparing tools, summarising </span><a href="https://www.uxdesigninstitute.com/blog/the-top-ux-design-trends-in-2024/"><span style="font-weight: 400;">UX industry trends</span></a><span style="font-weight: 400;">, and much, much more. </span></p>
<p><b>So what’s our final verdict on Perplexity AI and its role in the design process?</b></p>
<p><span style="font-weight: 400;">This is an AI tool well worth getting to grips with. Experiment with different prompts and use cases throughout your workflow to figure out when and where it’s most useful. And, as is the case with any AI tool, treat Perplexity as a super-smart assistant—not as a replacement for your own human knowledge, empathy, and better judgement. </span></p>
